title: Reader settings controls leak Material default colors and show orphan static labels
symptom: In the reader settings sheet, the brightness slider inactive track appears as the Material default purple, especially obvious in night mode, and the reading tab shows a standalone “护眼模式” label without a corresponding switch or action. The same theme-leak pattern also affected selected TTS choice pills because their text and selected backgrounds used MaterialTheme primary instead of the active reader palette.
root_cause: Reader settings controls had split styling paths. ReaderSettingsSheet used Material3 Slider without explicit reader-theme colors, so the control fell back to the app Material colorScheme instead of ReaderThemePalette. ReaderTtsSettingsSheet did not receive ReaderThemePalette at all, so selected voice/rate/pitch/timer pills read MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary. The brightness row also accepted a free trailingText label that was rendered as static text with no associated control.
fix: Set SliderDefaults.colors in ReaderSliderRow from ReaderThemePalette content colors for thumb, active track, and inactive track.
Remove the unused trailingText path and stop rendering the standalone “护眼模式” label.
Pass ReaderThemePalette into ReaderTtsSettingsSheet and render TTS status text, section labels, supporting text, and choice pills from the same reader palette.
Reuse ReaderInlinePill for TTS choices so reading/TTS selected pill colors have one shared implementation path.
Add an instrumented Compose test asserting the reading settings tab does not render the orphan eye-care label.
Add an instrumented pixel-capture regression test that sets Material primary to a trap color and asserts selected TTS choices do not render it.
failed_attempts: Relying on Material3 default Slider colors inside reader-themed sheets is unsafe; defaults can introduce unrelated app accent colors into day/night reader panels.
Checking settings behavior only by text presence misses color-theme regressions; pair tests with emulator screenshots for visual controls.
Treating the TTS settings body as a standalone Material surface repeats the same theme-leak class; reader overlay children need ReaderThemePalette explicitly, not ambient Material primary.
impact: Keeps reader settings and TTS controls visually consistent with day/night reading themes and removes a misleading non-interactive label.
